Tesla Bloomington Megacharger (world’s first full-scale public one for the Semi)Location: 18434 Valley Blvd, Bloomington, CA 92316 (San Bernardino County, ~1 hour east of LA, near key freight routes from the Ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach).  

Opened: ~July 17, 2026.  

Specs: 6 dedicated drive-thru stalls, each rated up to 1.2 MW (1,200 kW). Uses the Megacharger 2 (MC2) connector (MCS-compatible).  

Access: Open to all Tesla Semi customers. Large concrete lot designed for Class 8 trucks, with charging cabinets, light poles, and pull-through bays.

It’s Tesla’s first proper public Megacharger hub (replacing/superseding the earlier smaller Ontario test site). A Semi can add hundreds of miles of range in roughly 30 minutes here.

Grok 5: What it’s expected to bring

1. Massive scale

Mixture-of-Experts architecture in the 6–10 trillion parameter range. Big jump past the current ~1.5T Grok 4.x models. Training on the expanded Colossus 2 cluster.

2. Major leap in reasoning & agency

Stronger multi-step reasoning, better tool use, more reliable agents, and longer coherent planning. Elon previously put ~10% odds on early AGI-level performance. Official tone is more measured — big gains expected, true AGI still a high bar.

3. Native multimodality + real-time data

Built for text, images, audio, and video (including temporal understanding). Continues leveraging live X data for freshness and truth-seeking.

4. Efficiency focus

xAI is prioritizing speed and cost alongside scale. Expect strong performance-per-dollar for real work (coding, analysis, agents).

5. No fixed release date

Earlier targets slipped. Current stance: ships when it’s a real leap. Expected sometime in 2026. Intermediate 4.x updates continue in the meantime.

Starlink is no longer just for rural internet. 

• Home Internet Plans founder Tomas Novosad says Starlink is now being compared directly with cable, fiber, and fixed wireless providers.
• Consumers increasingly see Starlink as a legitimate option for its flexibility, availability, and reliability.
• Once viewed primarily as a solution for areas without wired broadband, Starlink is now competing in mainstream internet markets.
• Starlink now serves more than 12 million active customers across 160+ countries, territories, and other markets.

Starlink is evolving from a niche connectivity solution into a global broadband competitor.
